data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's evidence (monotonic increase in solution latency) cannot distinguish suppression from efficiency as the problem requires, because latency increase is fully predicted by ordinary forgetting or capacity saturation inside the owning lineage, with no suppression of cross-cutting explanations implied. Worse, its own countercondition concedes a case — 'Rival lineages solve problems instantly that the owner cannot solve at all' — that is exactly structural suppression of discovery, yet the target labels this merely 'structural suppression rather than delay' and excludes it from the latency test. So the test is silent precisely when suppression is most clear (owner never solves). Counting owner-only time-to-solution cannot observe rival primitives the owner is barred from using; it measures a learning curve, not suppression of cross-cutting reframings.
